holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Raisin Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the divisive but beloved movie-theater snack: plump raisins in a snug chocolate coat. Fans call it a sweet treat that feels almost like health food. Skeptics say it's a candy-aisle compromise. Pour a handful and decide which camp you're in.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its origin is unclear. It has appeared on March 24 on holiday calendars for years.
holidays.funFact: Raisins are just dried grapes, so each chocolate-covered raisin is technically a fruit dipped in chocolate.

holidays.name: National Cocktail Day
holidays.description: This is a day to raise a glass to the art of mixing drinks. You could shake up a classic Manhattan, try a zero-proof mocktail, or invent your own signature sip. Bartenders and home mixologists both get a chance to show off.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is sometimes confused with a similar cocktail day in May.
holidays.funFact: The word "cocktail" was defined in print in an 1806 New York publication as a mix of spirits, sugar, water, and bitters.

holidays.name: National Cheesesteak Day
holidays.description: This day honors the Philadelphia icon: thinly sliced beef, melted cheese, and a soft roll. Debates over the right cheese and whether to add onions are part of the fun. Grab a sandwich and join the argument.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It pays tribute to the sandwich that Philadelphia is famous for.
holidays.funFact: The cheesesteak is traditionally credited to Philadelphia hot dog vendor Pat Olivieri in the 1930s.
